questions.question: Which type of genetic material can be detected using real-time PCR for viral analysis?

explanations.a: Real-time PCR can also detect RNA after converting it to cDNA.
explanations.b: Real-time PCR can also detect DNA directly.
explanations.d: PCR amplifies nucleic acids, not proteins.

questions.question: What is the primary function of primers in PCR?

answers.b: To initiate DNA synthesis at specific target sites

explanations.a: Strands are separated by high temperature, not primers.
explanations.b: To initiate DNA synthesis at specific target sites.
explanations.c: Fluorescence is detected via dyes or labeled probes, not primers.
explanations.d: Primers do not affect the temperature of the reaction mixture.

questions.question: In PCR, the denaturation step is usually carried out to:

answers.b: Separate double-stranded DNA into single strands

explanations.a: Primer binding occurs during the annealing step.
explanations.b: Separate double-stranded DNA into single strands.
explanations.c: Synthesis occurs during the extension/elongation step.
explanations.d: Fluorescence data is recorded during extension/annealing, not denaturation.

questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for synthesizing DNA during PCR?

explanations.a: Reverse transcriptase converts RNA to cDNA, but Taq DNA polymerase replicates DNA during cycling.
explanations.b: Ligase seals nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone, it doesn't synthesize DNA.
explanations.d: Helicase unwinds DNA in cells, but PCR uses heat denaturation instead.

questions.question: In case of RNA viruses, why is reverse transcription necessary before qPCR?

explanations.a: We want to detect the RNA sequence, not destroy it.
explanations.c: Reverse transcription happens at moderate temperatures (e.g. 42-50 °C).
explanations.d: Primers bind to the template; reverse transcription is needed because DNA polymerase requires a DNA template.

questions.question: Which of the following is commonly included in a qPCR reaction mixture?

explanations.a: Agarose gel is used downstream to run conventional PCR products.
explanations.b: Ethanol is an inhibitor of PCR and is not added to the reaction mixture.
explanations.c: A fluorescent dye is used, but all other components like primers are also required.

questions.question: Real-time PCR differs from conventional PCR because it:

answers.b: Detects amplified product during each cycle

explanations.a: qPCR uses DNA polymerase just like conventional PCR.
explanations.b: Detects amplified product during each cycle.
explanations.c: Both qPCR and conventional PCR require primers.
explanations.d: Thermal cycling temperatures are highly similar between both techniques.

questions.question: Which stage of PCR allows primers to attach to the template DNA?

explanations.a: Denaturation separates DNA strands at high heat.
explanations.c: Extension is the phase where DNA polymerase builds the complementary strand.
explanations.d: Cooling is not a formal step of the PCR cycle; primer binding occurs specifically at the annealing temperature.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a fluorescent dye or probe in qPCR?

answers.c: To visualize amplification in real time

explanations.a: Dyes do not degrade or digest DNA.
explanations.b: Fluorescent molecules do not alter reaction temperature.
explanations.c: To visualize amplification in real time.
explanations.d: Separation of strands is achieved thermally.

questions.question: Which factor is most important for obtaining accurate qPCR results?

explanations.b: Reaction volume and tube size are minimized to improve thermal heat transfer.
explanations.c: Room temperature should be stable and comfortable, it does not dictate internal cycling conditions.
explanations.d: Tubes are typically transparent or white to allow optical fluorescence detection.
